title: Protecting Our Marine Spaces and Southern Islands
what_it_is: Protecting Our Marine Spaces and Southern Islands

sections.label: Singapore green initiatives
sections.summary: Singapore has several green plans and frameworks, including the Singapore Green Plan 2030 and Green Building Masterplan.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I am heartened to see that Singapore has become greener in all aspects of life.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: We now have the Singapore Green Plan 2030, the Singapore Green Building Masterplan, the Maritime Singapore Green Initiative, Singapore Green Bond Framework and the Singapore Green Finance Centre.

sections.label: Singapore marine ecosystem richness
sections.summary: Singapore has mangroves, mudflats, coral reefs, intertidal zones and seagrass meadows, with shares of global and regional species.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: We have a rich marine ecosystem of mangroves, mudflats, coral reefs, intertidal zones and seagrass meadows.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: We are home to 25% of the world's coral species, 55% of mangrove plants in Asia and 52% of seagrass species in the Indo-Pacific.

sections.label: Kunming-Montreal biodiversity framework adopted
sections.summary: The Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework was adopted at COP15 to conserve 30% of land, coastal areas and oceans by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: At last year's United Nations Biodiversity Conference (COP15), the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework was adopted to conserve 30% of the world's land, coastal areas and oceans by 2030.

sections.label: Mangrove carbon storage study
sections.summary: A 2015 study found Singapore's mangroves contain as much carbon as the annual emission of 620,000 people.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Looking at just our mangroves, a 2015 study found that they contain as much carbon as the annual emission of 620,000 people.

sections.label: Islands with marine park potential
sections.summary: Waters around Pulau Ubin, Pulau Semakau, Pulau Hantu, Pulau Jong, Pulau Biola, Pulau Satumu, St John's Island, Kusu Island and Lazarus Island are rich in biodiversity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The waters around the islands of Pulau Ubin, Pulau Semakau, Pulau Hantu, Pulau Jong, Pulau Biola, Pulau Satumu, St John’s Island, Kusu Island and Lazarus Island are all rich in biodiversity and have great potential as marine parks.

sections.label: Seagrass carbon capture and loss
sections.summary: Seagrasses capture carbon 35 times faster than tropical rainforests, but Singapore lost about half its seagrasses since the 1960s.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Seagrasses are 35 times faster than tropical rainforests in capturing carbon.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Despite their importance, we have lost 1.6 square kilometres or about half of our seagrasses since the 1960s.

sections.label: SG Blue Plan 2018 updates
sections.summary: Activists are asking for specific updates on the proposed recommendations in the SG Blue Plan 2018.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Lastly, Sir, activists are also asking for specific updates on the proposed recommendations in the SG Blue Plan 2018 which they called "a labour of love from civil society".

sections.label: Island visitorship and URA review
sections.summary: Island visitorship rose from 6,800 a month in 2019 to 17,000 in 2021, and URA's 2022 long-term plan review engaged over 13,000 participants.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Visitorship on the islands increased by 2.5 times, from 6,800 a month in 2019 to 17,000 a month in 2021.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In 2022, the Urban Redevelopment Authority (URA) conducted a long-term plan review (LTPR) and engaged more than 13,000 participants in polls, discussions and webinars, which culminated in roving exhibitions.

sections.label: Water quality near fish cages
sections.summary: It asks how the Government measures water and sediment quality and potential larger predators near fish cages 50 metres from Bendera Bay.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: How does the Government measure ongoing water and sediment quality as well as the potential presence of larger predators, given that the fish cages are barely 50 metres from Bendera Bay, which is stewarded by Friends of Marine Park?

sections.label: Conservation and development coordination
sections.summary: Balancing conservation and development requires tighter coordination among the many Government agencies managing the islands.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The balance between conservation and development requires tighter coordination between the multitude of Government agencies involved in the islands' management.

sections.label: Proposed inter-agency workgroup
sections.summary: It proposes an inter-agency workgroup, perhaps led by URA, to coordinate stakeholders and oversee island use, EIA's and development plans.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: While I appreciate the good work of each of these agencies, it may be difficult to have a holistic understanding of the islands' development and ensure that any changes are done sensitively.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I propose for an inter-agency workgroup with perhaps URA leading it to ensure systematic coordination between various stakeholders, utilising the technical expertise of each stakeholder.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: As recommended in the Singapore Blue Plan 2018, the inter-agency workgroup could then develop processes relating to the islands' use, implement a structured approach to manage competing land and ocean use, as well as oversee EIA's and the islands' development plans.

sections.label: EIA for Tiny Homes
sections.summary: It asks whether an EIA was conducted to understand and mitigate potential impact of new development such as Tiny Homes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Given that the Southern Islands are near marine and coastal areas, was an EIA conducted to understand and mitigate potential impact of the new development such as Tiny Homes on the area?

sections.label: Island carrying capacity research
sections.summary: The passage asks whether research exists to estimate the islands' carrying capacity and whether visitor numbers are capped.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Has there been any research to estimate the carrying capacity of the islands and are there limits or caps to the number of visitors on the island at any one point?

sections.label: Sewerage and waste plans
sections.summary: The passage asks whether sewerage treatment and waste disposal plans exist for increased human traffic and waste on the islands.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin
sentences.text: To provide sustainable living by powering houses through solar, building using sustainable materials and providing biogesters.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin
sentences.text: While efforts seek to lower the carbon footprint of tourists, are there any sewerage treatment and waste disposal plans to cope with the overall increased human traffic and corresponding waste generated on the islands?

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin
sentences.text: To be clear, this is not about no development, but an appeal for clear processes and frameworks to encourage a science-based and coordinated approach between Government agencies in doing so.

sections.label: Marine reef ecosystem fragility
sections.summary: The passage states that the marine and reef ecosystem takes years to develop but only a moment to destroy.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin
sentences.text: Our marine and reef ecosystem takes years to develop but only a moment to destroy if we do not prioritise them.

sections.label: Sisters' Islands Marine Park
sections.summary: The passage states that the Sisters' Islands Marine Park was established in 2014 for the area's ecological functions and marine life.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: In 2014, we established the Sisters’ Islands Marine Park, in view of the area’s important ecological functions and variety of marine life.

sections.label: Habitat restoration commitment increase
sections.summary: The passage states that an enhanced commitment was announced to restore and enhance 80 hectares of habitats by 2030, up from 30 hectares.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: At this year’s Committee of Supply debate, we announced our enhanced commitment to restore and enhance 80 hectares of habitats by 2030, up from 30 hectares previously.

sections.label: Marine Climate Change Science funding
sections.summary: The passage states that $25 million is being invested through the Marine Climate Change Science programme to address climate change impacts on marine ecosystems.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Through the Marine Climate Change Science programme, we are investing $25 million to develop solutions that address the impacts of climate change on our marine ecosystems.

sections.label: Ecological Profiling Exercise by NParks
sections.summary: NParks conducted an Ecological Profiling Exercise under the Long-Term Plan Review to understand Singapore's ecosystem and guide sensitive development.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: As part of the Long-Term Plan Review, NParks conducted an Ecological Profiling Exercise (EPE) to gain a more comprehensive understanding of Singapore’s island-wide ecosystem and ecological connectivity.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Based on the findings, NParks will work with agencies to study how development can be undertaken sensitively, taking into consideration the various habitats.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: For example, the marine EPE will help to guide future developments such as the placement of sea-based farms.

sections.label: Integrated Urban Coastal Management framework
sections.summary: An inter-agency committee developed the IUCM framework to guide planning and management of coastal and marine habitats and promote sustainable development.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: We engage nature groups and other stakeholders, so that their inputs can be considered in the review of our plans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: We have also developed an Integrated Urban Coastal Management (IUCM) framework that guides the planning and management of our coastal and marine habitats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: The framework is put together by an inter-agency committee including NParks, SFA, NEA, MPA and PUB, and seeks to promote the sustainable development of our coastal and marine areas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Agencies will continue to work closely together, for example, to monitor and coordinate responses to oil spill incidents as part of the IUCM framework.
